basis: Familial myoclonic epilepsy with cortical myoclonic tremor.
Hormone-secreting syndrome; persistent intestinal secretory dysfunction affects >70%. Cardiac lesions are occasional in supplied annotations; flushing alone does not establish skin damage.
Developmental spacing abnormality of the teeth; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Carcinoma arising in the duodenum.
Cardiac, skeletal and CNS malformations characterize embryopathy; renal hypoplasia/hydronephrosis annotated at 80-99%. Eye, ear and cleft-palate abnormalities omitted at cap.
Photosensitive brittle-hair disorder; intellectual disability 3/3, cataracts 2/3 and hearing impairment 1/3. GI and immune abnormalities have singleton evidence and are omitted at cap.
Tumour originates in the ovary, a reproductive organ; smooth-muscle histology does not establish skeletal-muscle involvement.
Ectopic ACTH causes cortisol excess; cortisol-mediated skeletal-muscle catabolism and proximal myopathy occur in roughly 40-60%. Tumour sites vary.
Mitochondrial metabolic cerebrohepatopathy defined by regression, seizures and hepatic failure. Cerebral visual impairment reflects brain injury, not ocular damage.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with developmental impairment, language delay, ataxia and variable seizures; ocular and hearing abnormalities are uncommon.
Substance-use disorder; infections and other organ injuries are separate complications rather than defining organ damage.
Lipid-associated granulomatous lesions predominantly affect sinonasal tissues. Altered erythrocytes within lesions do not establish a systemic blood disorder.
Mitochondrial oxidative-phosphorylation disorder causing spastic ataxia; optic atrophy occurs in 4/4 annotated patients.
Infant intestinal diarrheal disorder. Despite infectious ancestry, the definition and toddler-diarrhea synonyms encompass noninfectious disease, so infection is not universal.
Defined by severe insulin resistance and lipid abnormalities together with skeletal-muscle hypertrophy, weakness or myopathy.
Fatty-acid oxidation disorder with defining skeletal myopathy. Renal insufficiency occurs in 5/28, below the involvement threshold.
Folate-responsive megaloblastic anemia within an inherited folate-transport disorder; the immediate parent explicitly includes immunodeficiency. Hyperbilirubinemia reflects hemolysis.
Exencephaly combines exposed, malformed brain with absent or severely deficient cranial vault. Pituitary abnormalities are occasional; proptosis alone does not establish ocular damage.
Elevated circulating thyroxine; the umbrella includes euthyroid binding-protein abnormalities without consistent damage to other organs.
Congenital joint contractures and corpus-callosum agenesis define the disorder; optic atrophy occurs in 4/4 annotated patients.
Generalized subcutaneous fat loss with metabolic dysfunction; hepatic steatosis affects most patients and hepatomegaly occurs in 8/8. Cardiomyopathy is occasional.
Severe combined immunodeficiency; inflammatory erythroderma reported in 1/1 supports skin involvement. Pneumonia and autoimmune hemolytic anemia are separately diagnosed diseases.
Unilateral cerebral cortical malformation causing seizures and motor/developmental impairment. Ocular, hearing and vascular abnormalities are occasional.
Childhood motor peripheral neuropathy; muscle wasting reflects denervation rather than primary muscle disease. Cardiomyopathy occurs in 1/5, below threshold.
Inflammation of the diaphragm, a skeletal muscle. No lung, airway or pleural lesion or specific immune-mediated cause is established.
